transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-29 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Dana (Solstice Head of ML), Ravi (Solstice Dir Platform), Emily (Solstice Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may have errors): Customer is growing usage ahead of Q2 product launch, needs additional committed capacity and new regions. Interested in private VPC for certain workloads and wants to validate latency to EU and APAC. Procurement asked about contract amendment and billing cadence.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick roll call — we got dana, ravi, emily?
[00:08] Dana: yep hi thanks, running a bit late but here — hi maya, liam.
[00:11] Ravi: Ravi here.
[00:12] Emily: Emily on procurement, good to meet you.
[00:15] Maya: awesome. goal for today is a renewal/expansion check — you had signaled wanting to bump committed GPU capacity and add eu region, plus discuss contract term. want to confirm priorities and timeline.

[00:35] Dana: yeah the tl;dr: usage has spiked with our new triage feature, Q2 is our hard launch. we need about +30% committed capacity, and we need eu for residency and lower latency for our eu user subset. apac is optional but would like a pilot. also security is table stakes — SOC2, KMS, audit logs.

[00:58] Liam: thanks dana. when you say +30% committed, is that across all model classes, or concentrated on generation endpoints?
[01:06] Dana: mostly gen and chat endpoints; embeddings are steady. sequence lengths are similar but token volume per session up about 1.8x.

[01:20] Maya: ok good. ravi, from a platform POV any constraints — network, VPC, egress, anything that would push you to private deploy?
[01:28] Ravi: couple things — we need customer-managed KMS for keys holding pii-derived vectors; also strict audit logs and SSO integration. we prefer VPC for regulatory slices; but for burst traffic hosted would be easier. cost is a factor — our infra team is running the math comparing Redwood dedicated vs expanding our in-house gpu fleet.

[01:50] Maya: understood. we have two patterns that map: Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) with VPC peering and customer KMS, or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) for the most sensitive workloads. both support RBAC and audit logs. liam will walk through technicals.

[02:10] Liam: quick note — for KMS we support customer KMS via keywrap, and audit logs are available in the console or exported to your SIEM. for eu region, we can pin models to eu-only infra to satisfy residency. latency-wise, do you have target p99 numbers?

[02:28] Dana: p99 < 250ms for short chat contexts would be ideal. for longer sequences we accept more.

[02:36] Liam: ok that's helpful; baseline numbers I have for our eu nodes are typically p95 ~80-120ms for gpt-like small models, p99 varies with batch. we'll map precisely in the benchmark.

[02:50] Emily: quick procurement question — if we add committed capacity and extend the term, what's the cadence of billing and how do refunds or overage credits work?

[02:58] Maya: standard is monthly billing against committed units with overage charged at the discounted rate. for a 12-month extension we can provide a top-up discount — i'll put a proposal in writing.

[03:10] Ravi: also curious about the fallback behavior — if eu capacity exhausted, can requests failover to us-east or another region automatically? we need predictable SLA behavior.

[03:20] Liam: yes failover policies exist; you can configure routing policy per route — prefer eu, then fallback to us-east-dedicated. we also support automatic model variant fallback to a compatible quantized variant to keep latency up.

[03:38] Dana: are there any caveats for kv cache when failing over? we've seen cache miss storms in previous infra.

[03:44] Liam: good point. the runtime tries to preserve KV cache where possible but cross-region cold cache is expected. we recommend a warming plan in the runbook and sticky routing for sessions that need low latency. we'll include prefix caching options.

[04:05] Maya: ok let's get into the numbers — you mentioned +30% committed. do you want that as a flat top-up or phased across q2?

[04:12] Dana: phased is safer — +15% start of april, +15% start of june, but we'd like the option to burst if we need it.

[04:20] Maya: makes sense. we can do a phased top-up with burst capacity. for pricing that maps to a blended committed rate — i'll include two options in the amendment: immediate top-up vs phased with burst credits.

[04:35] Emily: for the contract extension, procurement prefers 12 months with the option to renegotiate at 9 months if usage differs significantly. is that something you can accommodate?

[04:44] Maya: yes we can add a 9-month review clause. i'm going to flag finance but that's a typical request.

[04:52] Ravi: about the apac pilot — we have users in sydney and singapore. latency from our tests to us-east is ~300-350ms which is borderline. what's the lead time to spin up an apac pilot region?

[05:06] Liam: for a pilot we can provision apac nodes within 3-4 weeks if capacity is available; procurement of dedicated hardware or private on-prem would be longer (6-8 weeks). for hosted we can do quicker.

[05:19] Dana: 3-4 weeks is fine for a pilot. can we do a short benchmark — maybe 1 day of synthetic traffic and 48 hours of production shadowing?

[05:28] Liam: yes we can run a staging benchmark plus a shadow period. i'll propose a test matrix: synthetic TTFB, throughput at 50/95/99 percentiles, and KV-cache warm/cold tests.

[05:40] Maya: perfect. let's talk about compliance items — SOC2 is confirmed on your side?

[05:46] Emily: (procurement) we need the SOC2 report or attestation and your retention policies. also need to know about KMS key lifecycle and whether Redwood ever sees plaintext.

[05:56] Liam: we hold SOC2 Type II; we can share the attestation under an NDA. regarding KMS, with customer-managed keys we do not have access to the unwrapped keys; key wrapping is used and logs show operations but not plaintext content. i'll include a short appendix on key lifecycle.

[06:15] Dana: are there any limits on model sizes when using quantized variants for cost savings? we've been experimenting with 70B models.

[06:23] Liam: we support quantized paths for many modern architectures; for 70B-class models you might see small quality regressions depending on the quantization profile. Redwood Optimize can run evals and suggest the right quantization level per workload.

[06:38] Dana: ok we'll need that in writing — quality/regression thresholds and rollback playbook.

[06:45] Maya: noted. liam, can we include a quality alert that triggers a rollback to original precision if eval metrics drop below X?

[06:52] Liam: yes, we can set automated rollback tied to eval thresholds and route to a higher-precision variant. playbook will be part of the runbook review.

[07:05] Emily: procurement question: can the amendment be an addendum to current MSA or do we need a new SOW?

[07:12] Maya: usually an amendment to the MSA plus a short SOW for the capacity and regions. i'll draft the amendment as an SOW addendum.

[07:20] Ravi: for benchmarks, can we bring a few of our own heavy prompts? the triage flows are pretty specific and synthetic traffic might not reflect them.

[07:26] Liam: absolutely — please share a sanitized prompt set or a representative harness; we can run with that. we have to be careful with PII — if you share real prompts, use test data or mask sensitive fields.

[07:38] Dana: we'll sanitize. next, on observability — do we get token-level cost breakdowns in console and per-route dashboards?

[07:46] Liam: yes per-route and per-model cost traces are available; also tracing hooks to link logs to your APM. retention for logs can be configured as an add-on.

[07:58] Maya: i'm going to propose a timeline: draft amendment this week, benchmark plan early next week, staging benchmark mid-next week, runbook review week after. does that match folks' expectations?

[08:09] Emily: timeline seems fine. we'll aim to make a procurement decision by 2027-02-15 if terms align.

[08:16] Dana: and go-live for phased capacity starting 2027-04-01 as discussed.

[08:22] Maya: great. any blockers?

[08:25] Ravi: only internal headcount to manage the runbook and approvals; i'll confirm owners by 2027-02-04.

[08:32] Liam: i'll start drafting the benchmark matrix and include warm/cold kv cache scenarios.

[08:37] Maya: ok quick pause — any competitor notes? dana mentioned internal gpu farm — any other vendors under consideration?

[08:45] Dana: we're also talking to VertexAI for eu coverage because they have regional presence but pricing isn't clear yet.

[08:51] Maya: understood. we'll send a cost/latency comparison for eu-hosted vs dedicated vs private so you can make an apples-to-apples comparison.

[09:00] (transcription artifact: some cross talk)
[09:05] Liam: technical note — if you move sensitive workloads to a private on-prem, latency will be best but ops overhead rises. hosted dedicated gives predictable throughput with less ops.

[09:18] Dana: right. for some parts of the pipeline we need private, for others hosted dedicated is fine. hybrid seems right.

[09:26] Maya: ok hybrid it is. let's put specific workloads in the runbook with routing policies.

[09:32] Emily: procurement needs a redlined SOW for review; ideally within 3 business days.

[09:36] Maya: i'll do 3 business days — expect draft by 2027-02-01 end of day.

[09:41] Ravi: one more technical Q — how do you handle KV cache eviction if multiple model variants in rotation? might cause oscillation.

[09:49] Liam: we have session affinity and prioritized eviction policies; the runbook will describe tuning knobs. in practice we avoid model variant churn during a session.

[10:00] (fast-forward, meeting continues; timestamps jump to key moments)
[29:12] Liam: benchmark plan overview: 4 tests — synthetic latency, throughput ramp, kv-warm vs cold, and resilience under region failover. we'll provide test harness and results dashboard.

[29:28] Dana: for resilience test, can we simulate eu outage and observe fallback within a 30s window? that's our SLA requirement.

[29:36] Liam: yes we can simulate and measure failover times and cache effects.

[30:05] Emily: about billing proration for phased top-up — do you prorate mid-month?

[30:12] Maya: standard practice is monthly proration based on start date; i'll detail examples in the amendment.

[31:00] Dana: any expected quality tradeoffs if we use quantized 8-bit paths for cost savings? we need a baseline A/B on our evaluation suite.

[31:08] Liam: expect slight lexical/semantic deltas — we'll run your eval suite and give delta metrics along with recommended thresholds for rollback.

[35:20] Maya: recap before we close: 1) Maya to send SOW amendment for 12-month extension with phased top-up options (due 2027-02-01) 2) Liam to share benchmark matrix and schedule staging test (due 2027-02-03) 3) Ravi to confirm runbook owners and share infra cost baseline (due 2027-02-04) 4) schedule 60-min technical runbook review week of 2027-02-07.

[35:50] Emily: that's accurate from procurement side.

[36:00] Dana: good call — excited to get the apac pilot running.

[36:05] Maya: thanks everyone. i'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.

[36:12] (meeting ends, recording stopped)
